subject: biology
title: Eukaryotic cell ultrastructure
key_idea: Eukaryotic cells have a nucleus and membrane-bound organelles, each with a job. Electron microscopes reveal their ultrastructure. Plant cells also have a cell wall, chloroplasts and a large vacuole. The rER and Golgi apparatus work together to make and export proteins.

blocks.text: All living organisms are made of cells with some common features: a cell surface membrane, cytoplasm, genetic material and ribosomes. Eukaryotic cells add a nucleus and other organelles.

items.meaning: The detailed structure of a cell seen with an electron microscope.
A structure inside a cell with a specific function, often surrounded by a membrane.
A cell whose DNA is held in a nucleus, with membrane-bound organelles.

diagram.alt: The organelles of eukaryotic cells. Tap each one to see its structure and function.
diagram.prompt: Tap an organelle to see its structure and function.

parts.name: Cell surface membrane
parts.detail: A phospholipid bilayer around the cell. It controls what enters and leaves.

parts.name: Nucleus
parts.detail: Surrounded by a double membrane (the nuclear envelope) with pores. It holds chromosomes of linear DNA bound to proteins, and one or more nucleoli that make ribosomal RNA and assemble ribosomes.

parts.name: Rough endoplasmic reticulum
parts.detail: Flattened, membrane-bound sacs with ribosomes on the surface. It makes proteins and folds them and carries them through the sacs.

parts.name: Smooth endoplasmic reticulum
parts.detail: Tubular membranes with no ribosomes. It makes and stores lipids and steroids and carbohydrates.

parts.name: Golgi apparatus
parts.detail: A stack of flattened sacs with vesicles. It modifies and packages proteins and makes lysosomes.

parts.name: Mitochondrion
parts.detail: A double membrane, with the inner one folded into cristae, around a matrix. It is the site of aerobic respiration, making ATP. It has small circular DNA and 70S ribosomes.

parts.name: Chloroplast
parts.detail: A double membrane around stroma and stacks of thylakoids called grana. It is the site of photosynthesis. It has small circular DNA and 70S ribosomes.

parts.name: Ribosome
parts.detail: A tiny structure of rRNA and protein, with no membrane. It makes proteins. They are 80S in the cytoplasm and on the rER, and 70S in mitochondria and chloroplasts.

parts.name: Lysosome
parts.detail: A membrane-bound sac of hydrolytic enzymes. It digests worn organelles and material taken into the cell.

parts.name: Centriole
parts.detail: A pair of hollow cylinders of microtubules near the nucleus in animal cells. They help to form the spindle in cell division.

parts.name: Cell wall
parts.detail: A rigid layer outside the membrane of plant and algal cells (made of cellulose) and fungal cells (made of chitin). It supports the cell and stops it bursting.

parts.name: Vacuole
parts.detail: A large permanent sac in plant cells, surrounded by a membrane called the tonoplast. It holds cell sap and keeps the cell turgid.

items: Many organelles are surrounded by a membrane, so a cell can keep different reactions in separate compartments.
Mitochondria and chloroplasts have a double membrane, their own circular DNA and 70S ribosomes.
Specialised cells are organised into tissues, tissues into organs and organs into systems.
Learn each organelle's structure and its link to its function.
Cells with a specific job have more of the organelles that job needs.

blocks.text: Some cells have extra structures that suit their job.

items: **Cilia** are short, hair-like projections that beat to move fluid or mucus over the cell surface.
**Flagella** are longer, whip-like projections that beat to move the whole cell, for example a sperm.
**Microvilli** are tiny finger-like folds of the membrane that increase its surface area for absorption.
**Plasmodesmata** are narrow channels through plant cell walls, which link the cytoplasm of neighbouring cells.
**Microtubules** are hollow protein tubes. They make up centrioles, cilia, flagella and the spindle, and vesicles and organelles move along them.
**Pits** are thin areas of the wall where many plasmodesmata are found.
Cilia and flagella move things; microvilli increase surface area.
Plasmodesmata let substances pass between plant cells.

blocks.text: Plant and animal cells share many organelles. Plant cells also have structures linked to support and photosynthesis.

rows: Present, made of cellulose, with a middle lamella of pectin between cells
Present in cells exposed to light
Present in storage cells, where they store starch
Large and permanent, with a tonoplast

items: Both have a nucleus, rough and smooth ER, Golgi apparatus, mitochondria, ribosomes, lysosomes and a cell surface membrane.
The **middle lamella** is a layer of pectin that glues neighbouring plant cells together.
Plant cells have a wall, chloroplasts and a large vacuole; animal cells do not.
Both types have a nucleus, mitochondria, ER, Golgi apparatus and ribosomes.

blocks.text: Several organelles work in order to make a protein, process it and release it from the cell. Digestive enzymes released from cells are called extracellular enzymes.

diagram.alt: The route of a protein from nucleus to the outside of the cell.
steps: DNA in the nucleus is copied into mRNA
Ribosomes on the rER make the protein
Protein enters the rER and is folded
Vesicle carries protein to the Golgi
Golgi modifies and packages the protein
Secretory vesicle fuses with the membrane and releases the protein

items: mRNA leaves the nucleus through a pore and attaches to a ribosome on the rER.
The protein passes into the inside of the rER, where it is folded into its shape.
A piece of rER pinches off as a **vesicle** and carries the protein to the Golgi apparatus.
The Golgi modifies the protein, for example by adding a carbohydrate, and packages it in a secretory vesicle.
The vesicle moves to the cell surface membrane and fuses with it, releasing the protein by **exocytosis**.
Some Golgi vesicles stay in the cell as lysosomes.
Order: nucleus, ribosome on rER, rER, vesicle, Golgi, vesicle, cell surface membrane.
Cells that secrete a lot of protein have a lot of rER and Golgi.

blocks.text: In a TEM image, you recognise an organelle by its shape, its membranes and its size. Learn the clues below.

rows: Large and round, with a double envelope with gaps (pores) and darker chromatin inside
Oval or rod shape, double membrane with inner folds (cristae)
Larger oval, with stacks of discs (grana) and often starch grains
Flattened sacs studded with tiny dark dots (ribosomes)
Tubes and sacs with no dots
Curved stack of flattened sacs, with small vesicles at the edges
Small, round, dense, with a single membrane
Thick layer outside the cell surface membrane

items: A TEM shows a thin slice, so the same organelle may look round, oval or long, depending on the angle of the cut.
An SEM shows the outside surface in 3D.
Use the scale bar or the magnification to work out the real size.
Use membranes, folds and dots on the surface to name organelles.
A slice through an organelle can look different depending on the cut.

checks.q: Describe the structure of a mitochondrion and state its function.
checks.a: It has a double membrane, with the inner membrane folded into cristae, around a matrix; it contains small circular DNA and 70S ribosomes. It is the site of aerobic respiration, making ATP.

checks.q: Describe the route taken by a protein that is made on the rER and secreted from the cell.
checks.a: Made on ribosomes on the rER and folded inside it; carried in a vesicle to the Golgi apparatus; modified and packaged in a secretory vesicle; the vesicle fuses with the cell surface membrane and releases the protein by exocytosis.

checks.q: State three structures found in a plant cell but not in an animal cell.
checks.a: Any three from: cellulose cell wall, chloroplasts, large permanent vacuole with tonoplast, plasmodesmata, pits, amyloplasts.

blocks.text: The cytoskeleton is a network of protein fibres in the cytoplasm. It has three jobs.

items: It gives **mechanical strength** to the cell and helps it keep its shape.
It aids **transport** inside cells: vesicles and organelles move along microtubules, driven by motor proteins.
It enables **cell movement**: it moves cilia and flagella, and changes the shape of the cell in amoeboid movement.
Microtubules also make the spindle in cell division.

blocks.text: The interrelationship of organelles is the route in the protein pathway: nucleus, rER, vesicle, Golgi, vesicle, cell surface membrane.
